source_identity.canonical_title: Une femme au foyer peut être parfaitement épanouie

translation.canonical_title: A housewife can be perfectly fulfilled
translation.displayed_title: A housewife can be perfectly fulfilled
translation.summary: A movement inspired by the 50s and called #tradwife (or traditional housewife) advocates a femininity fulfilled through domestic work and caring for one’s husband and family. It is an extension of a similar movement called “fascinating womanhood,” theorized by Helen Andelin in 1967. Antifeminist, this current promotes traditional values based on a mutual exchange: motherhood, household tasks and moral support attributed to the woman in return for household security and financial support attributed to the man. It then appears unnecessary or even dangerous for a housewife to venture outside to work, a source of distraction and stress when all she needs is at home. The movement claims to restore a healthy balance between men and women in accordance with their biological attributes.

citations.translated_citation: This means recognizing the man as the head of the family and therefore using one’s talents and abilities to serve him, in the same way that the man serves his wife by going to work and providing for all the household’s material needs. It is also expressed through the appreciation and pride he feels toward his wife
